card_summary: The proliferation of video wall technology suggests a growing need for low-latency, high-bandwidth signal transport. In live production, this typically means leveraging ST 2110 and NMOS for real-time transport, ensuring frame-accuracy and signal integrity. For high-end applications, 12G-SDI and JPEG XS might be the preferred choice, offering the necessary bandwidth and compression efficiency. Meanwhile, SRT and RIST protocols are gaining traction for their ability to maintain low-latency over IP networks. In practice, this means engineering teams must carefully balance signal quality with network constraints. As video walls become more prevalent, the risk of latency-induced artifacts or signal degradation increases. To mitigate this, teams should prioritize ST 2110's built-in latency monitoring and adjust their network architecture accordingly. Furthermore, incorporating Genlock and AES67 for synchronization and audio transport will be crucial for maintaining a cohesive, low-latency signal chain.

Why Broadcasters Must Rethink Signal Transport for Live Video Walls

Live video walls are no longer a novelty, but a staple in modern broadcasting. With the rise of remote production, social distancing, and the need for greater flexibility in live event coverage, video walls have become an essential tool for broadcasters. However, the technology behind these video walls is forcing a reevaluation of traditional signal transport methods. The shift towards IP-based signal transport, driven by standards like ST 2110, is gaining momentum, and broadcasters must adapt to ensure seamless integration and minimal latency.

What This Development Actually Means

Haivision, a leading provider of video networking and intelligent media solutions, has announced significant advancements in its video wall technology, leveraging the power of ST 2110 to deliver low-latency, high-quality video transport over IP networks. This move marks a crucial step towards the widespread adoption of IP-based signal transport in live broadcasting, enabling broadcasters to transition away from traditional baseband and fiber-optic infrastructures.

This development is a response to the growing demand for greater flexibility and scalability in live event coverage. As broadcasters continue to push the boundaries of remote production, social distancing, and virtual events, the need for a more agile and efficient signal transport method has become increasingly pressing.

Why It Matters for Broadcast Operations

The shift towards IP-based signal transport will have far-reaching implications for broadcast operations. For one, it will enable broadcasters to significantly reduce their CapEx and OpEx costs associated with traditional baseband and fiber-optic infrastructures. With ST 2110, broadcasters can leverage existing IP networks, eliminating the need for dedicated fiber-optic cables and reducing the overall cost of signal transport. Furthermore, IP-based signal transport will simplify signal routing and management, allowing broadcasters to easily scale their operations to meet the demands of live events.

Harmonic VOS360, a leading OTT origin and delivery platform, is already integrating ST 2110 into its architecture, enabling broadcasters to take advantage of low-latency, high-quality video transport over IP networks. Similarly, Telestream Vantage, a renowned video processing and delivery platform, is also embracing ST 2110, providing broadcasters with a seamless transition to IP-based signal transport.
